items.title: Jang interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2013
items.q: And Chou En-lai, who studied in the west, studied in Paris, was friends with W.E.B. Debois

ctx.x: Because well we see Min Xiao-Fen is performing with me on pipa. And when Chinese come over here there’s that social interaction, the musical interaction, and then they become sort of the modern Chinese-born American. Whereas, and you could see, well I’ll give you an example of two great leaders: Mao Tse Tung, okay? So there’s a story about one of the Chinese saxophonists who was older than me by about twenty years, who performed for Mao. And Chou En-lai, who studied in the west, studied in Paris, was friends with…

Well last week, timely, there was a couple of Chinese students. I’m not even sure they were teaching assistants, they did an hour program on Chinese popular music. One did something she called Chinese rock & roll. And the other one did, and I wish I had written the word down, there was a term that apparently there’s a popular style that combines almost hip hop, that kind of thing, using traditional Chinese instruments. It was very interesting. And it’s amazing how pervasive Western pop music is now around the…

items.title: Jon Jang interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 17, 2003 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: W.E.B. DuBois said that, with their brawn and sweat.

ctx.x: Oh well it’s like Max Roach he told me he said I can’t save the world. I mean he’s lived such a full life and you kind of see the roller coaster and the changing trends. I don’t know you know part of it is I guess being a Christian you have faith. And sometimes, well I guess the recording that David Murray and I did called “River of Life” and that’s from Revelations I think it’s 21 or 22. And I think let’s see if I can recall the scriptures, it says, “Then the angel showed me the river of the water of life, as…

with I think water or tears flowing down. It’s just like the “River of Life” on the piano. I think he was trying to play some hymn, “Peace in the Valley” or something. I don’t remember. But all of a sudden this peace blossom. Take my hand precious Lord. And it’s just such a moving piece because it’s like being in sea where there’s calmness and then there’s that storm and it hits that high pitch. And I forgot where I heard Marion Williams, when I used to perform in an African-American church that was a song that…
